_comment: Normative constants for the RoboTensor one-demonstration in-context imitation learning competition. Version 4 was published and then rolled back; that number is retired and never reused. Version 5 splits the competition into fields: each has its own demonstration modality, skills, pool, baseline, king, queue and lineage. Bumping spec_version changes every derived duel id.

sensorimotor.title: Sensorimotor demonstration
sensorimotor.blurb: The model is shown one demonstration - the frames, the action trajectory and the proprioception - and must do the task from the initial scene it was shown.
sensorimotor._comment: Renamed from the v3 track id 'icil_1demo'. At v6 this field runs on RoboTwin, because the orchestrator ships no benchmark of its own and RoboTwin is the one that is plugged. RoboTwin V1 implements only `same_scene`, so this field is Same Scene WITH the action trajectory - and that combination is degenerate: replaying the demonstration's own actions into the identical scene solves the episode, and the benchmark's replay oracle scores 18/18 doing exactly that. So this field no longer closes the replay shortcut at all, and its scores must not be read as if it did. It is honest only as a measurement of what a model does when copying is available to it, and as the path that exercises the orchestration while the video-only field has no trained checkpoint. Restoring a real sensorimotor field needs a benchmark that can score from a different initial state; `prompt_instance_disjoint` is false here because it must be, not because the field was designed that way.
sensorimotor._sizes_comment: A RoboTwin unit is a scene build, an expert demonstration and a rollout of up to 900 steps, so a smoke duel is one unit per skill: six rollouts across both sides. The size names are the same vocabulary every field shows a submitter; only the counts differ.

video_only.title: Video-only demonstration
video_only.blurb: The model is shown one demonstration as frames only - no action trajectory, no proprioception - and must do the task from the identical initial scene.
video_only._comment: Same Scene: the demonstration starts in the very scene the rollout is scored in, so replaying its actions would be perfect - which is exactly why they are withheld, and why this field and the sensorimotor one close the same shortcut in opposite ways. Its prompts are materialized per duel and published with the event rather than up front, because a demonstration of the scored scene is the answer for it. Sizes are small and the void tolerance higher: a unit is a scene rebuild plus a rollout, and a rebuild that drifts is the benchmark's fault rather than the model's.

robotwin._comment: Pinned by distribution, version and wheel sha256 once published: entry-point discovery imports code into the validator, so what it may import is part of the contract.

_benchmarks_comment: Every benchmark is a separate distribution found through the `icilval.benchmarks` entry point group. The orchestrator ships none: what it can score is exactly what is plugged into it.

rt_sm_pick_and_place.title: Pick and place (RoboTwin)
rt_sm_pick_and_place.blurb: Grasp one object and place it somewhere: RoboTwin's place_a2b_left, place_a2b_right, place_empty_cup and place_container_plate. The model is shown one demonstration - frames, the action trajectory and proprioception - and is then scored from the identical initial scene. RoboTwin 2.0's own expert produces the demonstration at evaluation time and its own check decides the outcome.

environment._comment: The camera profile replaces one static camera in its slot; every static camera draws from numpy's RNG before the scene is built, so adding or removing one would move every seed's scene where the fingerprint cannot see it. far_side is what the BPP adapter was measured with. `action_type: ee` is the 16-number bimanual end-effector command RoboTwin's `take_action` accepts, not the 14-dim qpos.

rt_sm_stacking.blurb: Put one object on another and leave it standing: RoboTwin's stack_blocks_two and stack_bowls_two. rt_pick_and_place.title: Pick and place (RoboTwin)
rt_pick_and_place.blurb: Watch one demonstration of a bimanual pick and place, as frames only, then do it from the identical initial scene. RoboTwin 2.0's own expert produced the demonstration and its own check decides the outcome.

skill_encoder._comment: Organizer-owned and frozen: the skill encoder is a preprocessor in the validator's image, not part of a submission, so two entrants are comparable and nobody can smuggle capability into it. sha256 is pinned when the architecture template is emitted.

rt_stacking.title: Stacking (RoboTwin)
rt_stacking.blurb: Watch one demonstration of stacking two objects, as frames only, then do it from the identical initial scene. The longest-horizon of the three, so its step cap is the highest.

skill_encoder._comment: Organizer-owned and frozen: the skill encoder is a preprocessor in the validator's image, not part of a submission, so two entrants are comparable and nobody can smuggle capability into it. sha256 is pinned when the architecture template is emitted.

rt_press_push.title: Press and push (RoboTwin)
rt_press_push.blurb: Watch one demonstration of pressing or pushing something, as frames only, then do it from the identical initial scene. The shortest-horizon of the three.

pools._comment: Kept for a future field whose prompts are drawn from a pool built offline. Both fields at v6 materialize their prompts per duel, so no pool is built or pinned.

duel._crown_comment: Both sides run the identical unit list (same tasks, initial states, prompt demonstrations and seeds). Per-skill success rate is stored as a fraction in [0, 1]; the final score is the mean over skills. A skill's units are spread evenly over its eligible tasks. The challenger takes the crown iff challenger.average >= king.average + score_margin / 100. Paired per-unit outcomes are published as a diagnostic and never decide the crown.
duel._max_steps_comment: skills.<skill>.max_steps are per-skill caps; each task carries its own (smaller) limit from its source benchmark.
duel._default_comment: Defaults. A track may override sizes, score_margin or max_void_fraction; an override must declare the same size names, so a submitter sees one vocabulary.

model._comment: A submission is a Hugging Face model repo holding one directory per skill, each with model.safetensors and config.yaml. For every skill the validator instantiates the architecture from its own allow-listed template (arch/<architecture>.cfg.json), diffs the submitted config against it, checks the safetensors header against arch/<architecture>.tensors.json, and loads weights strictly. No pickle is ever read and no entrant code runs. max_params applies per skill; max_repo_bytes to the whole repo.
model._mutable_comment: Dotted paths under `model` that may differ from the template without affecting inference. Training-only keys are overwritten by the converter, so they never differ.

media._comment: resolution and camera describe LIBERO clips; draw clips are the board render at skills.draw_anything.environment.render_resolution and draw demonstration clips are the 224 px observation frames.

store._layout_comment: manifest.json; tracks/{track}/{head.json,queue.json,index-NNNN.jsonl}; events/{track}/{event_id}.json; media/{sha[:2]}/{sha}.mp4. Index lines are '<canonical_json>\t<ed25519_signature_hex>', append-only.

baselines._comment: Both thrones are empty at v6. The sensorimotor field's v5 genesis was BPP on LIBERO and DrawAnything, which are no longer scored here; a genesis on the RoboTwin skills has to be published before there is a king. The protocol already handles an empty throne: the first entrant is crowned by genesis.
